# Easy Modbus

> Free Android app that finds Modbus TCP and Modbus RTU-over-TCP equipment on a
> local network, helps work out what its registers mean, saves that register map,
> and exports it as CSV. Published with a set of plain-English Modbus guides
> written for facility managers and building engineers rather than for protocol
> specialists.

The guides below each answer one question directly in their first paragraph and
are free to quote with attribution.

## Free tools

- [Modbus float and byte-order decoder](https://easymodbus.com/modbus-float-decoder): Paste two Modbus registers and see the 32-bit float and integer in all four word orders (ABCD, CDAB, BADC, DCBA). Free, runs in your browser, nothing uploaded.
- [Modbus address converter](https://easymodbus.com/modbus-address-converter): Convert any Modbus address between Modicon (40001), prefixed (4x00001), 1-based and 0-based forms. Shows the register table and function code. Free tool.

## Guides

- [What is Modbus?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/what-is-modbus): Modbus is a simple protocol for reading and writing numbered registers on industrial and building equipment. What it is, in plain English.
- [What is a Modbus register map?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/what-is-a-modbus-register-map): A Modbus register map ties each address to what it means: data type, scaling, word order and units. What it contains and why you need one.
- [How do I find my Modbus register map?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/how-to-find-modbus-register-map): Build a Modbus register map from a live device: read blocks, decode each value's type and scaling, name it, and export the map as a CSV.
- [Why is my Modbus address off by one?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-address-off-by-one): 40001, 4x00001, register 1 and address 0 are all the same Modbus register. Here is why the conventions conflict, and how to tell which one your document uses.
- [Why does my Modbus value look wrong?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-value-wrong-scaling-byte-order): A Modbus value that reads wrong is usually scaling or byte/word order. How to spot 32-bit floats, word swaps and multipliers, and fix them.
- [Why can't I find my Modbus devices on the network?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/cannot-find-modbus-devices): Modbus has no discovery at all — devices never announce themselves. Here is why scanning is the only option, and the six things to check when nothing answers.
- [Modbus TCP, Modbus RTU or RS-485 — which do I have?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-tcp-vs-rtu-vs-rs485): How to tell Modbus TCP from Modbus RTU and RTU-over-TCP by looking at the equipment, and why mistaking one for the other looks exactly like a dead device.
- [What is a Modbus unit ID or slave ID?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-unit-id-slave-id): The Modbus unit ID (slave ID) picks which device answers on a shared line or gateway. What it is, why it matters, and how to find the right one.
- [What are Modbus function codes?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-function-codes-explained): Function codes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 15 and 16 explained in plain English, plus what each exception code means when a device refuses a request.
- [Is it safe to write to a Modbus register?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/is-it-safe-to-write-to-modbus): Modbus writes take effect instantly and have no undo. What that means, when writing is safe, and how Easy Modbus reduces the risk.
- [A vendor asked for my Modbus information — what do I send?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/vendor-asking-for-modbus-information): What to hand a vendor or integrator who asks for your Modbus details: IP, unit ID, and a full register map with types and scaling, exported as a CSV.
- [What is the difference between Modbus and BACnet?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-vs-bacnet): Modbus sends bare 16-bit values and explains nothing; BACnet describes itself with names, units and discovery. What that means for integration.
- [Why is my Modbus reading slow or unreliable?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-reading-slow-or-unreliable): Slow or intermittent Modbus reads: block sizes, serial turnaround, connection limits, polling collisions and stale replies, and how to fix each.
- [How do I use Easy Modbus to read values from a Modbus device?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/how-to-use-easy-modbus): Step by step: find or add the device, test the connection, add your first reading with the Easy wizard, and export the register map with live values.
- [How do I write to a Modbus register with Easy Modbus, and put it back afterwards?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/how-to-write-to-a-modbus-register): How to safely write a value to a Modbus register, confirm it against a summary, and put the register back the way you found it.
- [How do I build a custom remote for a Modbus device in Easy Modbus?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/how-to-build-a-modbus-remote): Build a drag-and-drop control screen for one Modbus device: readouts, setpoints, toggles and a restore button. The free one-remote limit explained.
- [What is a good free alternative to Modbus Poll?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-poll-alternative): Modbus Poll is a paid Windows master. If you want a free tool, or one that runs on your phone in front of the equipment, here are the honest trade-offs.
- [Is there a Modbus scanner app for Android?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-scanner-app-android): Yes. How to scan for, read and write Modbus TCP equipment from an Android phone, what a phone can and cannot reach, and the RTU-over-gateway catch.
- [Why is my Modbus request timing out with no response?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-timeout-no-response): A Modbus timeout means your request left but nothing came back. The seven causes in order of likelihood, and how to tell a network fault from a framing one.
- [What do Modbus exception codes mean?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-exception-codes): Modbus exception codes 01, 02, 03, 04, 06, 0A and 0B in plain English: what each means, what caused it, and the fix. Exception 02 is almost always addressing.
- [What causes a Modbus CRC error, and how do I fix it?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-crc-error): A Modbus CRC error means the message arrived corrupted. The real causes: noise, termination, baud mismatch, and RTU/TCP framing confusion, and how to fix each.
- [Modbus Poll vs Easy Modbus — which should I use?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-poll-vs-easy-modbus): A straight comparison of Modbus Poll and Easy Modbus: platform, price, reading, writing, data-type decoding and simulation, with a clear rule for choosing.
- [Why does my Modbus register read 0?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-register-reads-zero): A Modbus register reading 0 is usually the wrong function code, an off-by-one address, or a value split across two registers, not a dead device.
- [What does Modbus connection refused (Errno 111) mean?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-connection-refused): Connection refused means something is at that IP but nothing listens on the Modbus port. The causes (wrong port, Modbus off, wrong host, limit) and fixes.
- [How do I log Modbus data to CSV, and trend a register over time?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/log-modbus-to-csv-on-phone): How to record Modbus register values to a CSV you can open in Excel, from a phone with no laptop or SCADA, and what to capture to make the log useful.
- [How do I find an unknown Modbus device's baud rate and parity?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/find-modbus-baud-rate-parity): No display, no paperwork, and a serial Modbus device that won't answer? How to find the baud rate, parity and unit ID by trying the few combinations that occur.
- [How do I get around the Modbus Poll 10-minute trial limit?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/modbus-poll-10-minute-limit): Modbus Poll's trial disconnects after 10 minutes until you buy a licence. To just read or write registers, Easy Modbus is free with no timer.
- [How do I read an Eastron SDM power meter over Modbus?](https://easymodbus.com/guides/read-eastron-sdm-modbus): Eastron SDM120/SDM220/SDM630 meters report each value as a 32-bit float over Modbus. The settings, function code, word order, and how to read them from a phone.

## About the app

- Platform: Android 8.0 or later. Free with rewarded ads (AdMob) removable by one-time purchase; no account, no analytics.
- Protocols: Modbus TCP and Modbus RTU over TCP, function codes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6,
  15, 16, and 43/14 device identification.
- Finds equipment by sweeping the local subnet for open port 502, because Modbus
  has no discovery mechanism.
- Decodes INT16, UINT16, INT32, UINT32, FLOAT32, INT64, UINT64, FLOAT64, single
  bits within a register, and packed ASCII, in ABCD, CDAB, BADC and DCBA word
  order, with per-reading multiplier and offset.
- Accepts addresses in Modicon (40007), prefixed (4x00007), one-based and
  zero-based forms, and explains how it read them.
- Writes are off by default and off again at every launch; each write is
  confirmed, bounded by per-reading limits, read back afterwards, and logged.

## Key facts about Modbus that these guides cover

- Modbus has no discovery: devices never announce themselves, so finding them
  requires sweeping addresses.
- Modbus carries no data types, names, or units. A register is sixteen bits and
  the meaning exists only in vendor documentation.
- The same register is written as 40001, 4x00001, "register 1" and "address 0" by
  different documents. Off-by-one addressing is the most common single mistake.
- In Modbus documentation "0x" denotes the coil table, not hexadecimal.
- Values spanning two registers come in four word orders; CDAB is very common on
  power meters and drives.
- Reporting tenths in a 16-bit integer is the most widespread scaling convention.
- Writes have no undo, no timeout, and no priority system. A written value stays
  written until something overwrites it.
- An exception reply proves a device is present and reachable; only silence means
  absent.
